about: Deliberate breaks from NES limits in GATSBY.EXE. Entries with a rule the checker reports (BG-CELL, BG-PALS, SPR-TILE, SPR-PALS, SCANLINE) excuse matching violations (scene/where take * wildcards). Entries with rule DESIGN describe what the checker leaves out by design. Explained in docs/gatsby/hardware.md.

exceptions.what: Parallax backgrounds are separate planes behind the tile plane, each checked on its own 16px grid
exceptions.why: The NES has one background plane; parallax needs raster splits in bands with nothing else in them. Each plane still obeys the attribute rule and shares the stage's four background palettes and backdrop.

exceptions.what: Vehicles, the couch, the piano and the Eckleburg billboard move like sprites but are held to the background rules (16x16 areas, background palettes) and left out of the sprite count
exceptions.why: Each is wider than eight sprites can show on a line. A real cart would draw them into the background, as Mega Man 2 does with its biggest bosses, which only works with a plain background behind them.

exceptions.what: The HUD's text, message boxes, the pause screen's dimming, fades, the white flash and the Argonne's darkness are drawn over the play area
exceptions.why: On hardware these would be a status bar or window (a split) and palette fades. The HUD's hearts and icons are sprites and are counted.

exceptions.what: Falling ash (II), the heat haze (VII) and the mist (IX) are drawn as a screen effect, not as sprites
exceptions.why: Hundreds of specks would be far over the sprite limit; a real game would animate background tiles instead.
